name: Samsung Pyeongtaek P5
summary: The fifth line at Samsung's Pyeongtaek campus, in the site's second complex. Korean press reported that work on P5 stopped, along with parts of P4, from early 2024 during the memory downturn. In November 2025 Samsung said a management committee had decided to proceed with the building's frame construction, aiming for full operation in 2028, as part of a group pledge of KRW 450 trillion in domestic investment over five years. In August 2026 trade press reported foundation work on two fab units, P5-1 and P5-2, meant for HBM and other DRAM, V-NAND and foundry chips, with final completion targeted for 2030, and a pending planning amendment that would allow a larger triple-fab layout.

location.note: In the second complex of the Pyeongtaek campus.

milestones.note: TrendForce dates the start of P5 construction to 2022.
Reported stalled with P4 from early 2024; in June 2025 the city said it had received no recent permit requests for P5.
Samsung announced on 16 November 2025 that a recent management committee meeting had approved proceeding with the frame construction; the meeting date is not given.
Full-scale operation target set when construction was approved to proceed.
Final completion target reported in August 2026, while foundation work for P5-1 and P5-2 was under way.

notes: No P5-specific investment figure is given in the cited sources; the KRW 450 trillion pledge covers Samsung group companies' domestic spending including R&D. Status evidence is from press and trade-press reports rather than a Samsung release. TrendForce reported that Samsung had applied to raise the site's floor area ratio from 350% to 490%, which would allow a triple-fab layout with up to six cleanrooms; approval was pending in August 2026.
